Class IpfFhirConfigurationProperties.StreamingUpload

java.lang.Object
org.openehealth.ipf.boot.fhir.IpfFhirConfigurationProperties.StreamingUpload
Enclosing class:
IpfFhirConfigurationProperties
public static class IpfFhirConfigurationProperties.StreamingUpload extends Object
Configuration of the streaming upload split, i.e. this starter's half of the bridge to Base64SplittingFilter. The split itself knows nothing about Spring or about this starter; everything it needs is handed to it as StreamingUploadOptions.

    • getEngageAboveBytes

      public int getEngageAboveBytes()
      Only request bodies larger than this are split; smaller ones are passed through byte for byte, so that ordinary requests behave exactly as they do without this filter.

      This is measured on the whole request body, i.e. metadata plus the base64 of all documents in it.

    • setEngageAboveBytes

      public void setEngageAboveBytes(int engageAboveBytes)
      Only request bodies larger than this are split; smaller ones are passed through byte for byte, so that ordinary requests behave exactly as they do without this filter.

      This is measured on the whole request body, i.e. metadata plus the base64 of all documents in it.

    • getMemoryThresholdBytes

      public int getMemoryThresholdBytes()
      Extracted document content up to this size is kept in memory instead of being written to a temporary file.

      This is measured on a single decoded document and is therefore deliberately independent of engageAboveBytes; it is quite normal for it to be the larger of the two. Splitting the body is what avoids the expensive part - the base64 text and the decoded array that the FHIR parser would otherwise materialize - whereas a temporary file is only needed to also avoid a large contiguous heap allocation. Small documents therefore stay in memory and cause no disk I/O at all.

    • getInlineDocumentResources

      public Set<String> getInlineDocumentResources()
      Types of the resources whose create interaction carries a document inline. Defaults to what MHD needs, i.e. the ITI-105 create of a DocumentReference; a POST to the FHIR base itself, such as the ITI-65 transaction bundle, is always considered regardless of this setting.

    • setInlineDocumentResources

    • getFilterOrder

      public int getFilterOrder()
      Order of the filter in the servlet filter chain. The default places it directly after the Spring Security filter chain, whose own default order is -100: unauthenticated requests must never be spooled to disk, and any request logging registered further down then sees the slimmed-down body rather than buffering the full upload a second time. The value is spelled out rather than derived from Spring Boot's SecurityProperties.DEFAULT_FILTER_ORDER, which this starter does not depend on.
